summary:
ChacraSat is a free, bilingual (English/Spanish) web decision-support tool that transforms NASA Earth observations into actionable 18-month crop rotation plans for small and medium farmers on Peru’s northern desert coast. Around Trujillo (La Libertad), rainfall covers only ~6% of annual crop water demand (92 mm rain vs. 1,430 mm ETo), while sudden El Niño events bring extreme heat (+3.2 °C) and flash floods. Meanwhile, continuous monocropping depletes nutrients and increases soil salinity. 

  By integrating real NASA POWER satellite data (MERRA-2/GEOS, CERES: temperature, rainfall, and root-zone soil wetness) with FAO-56 water demand and FAO-29 salinity thresholds, ChacraSat evaluates 2-to-3 crop sequences across five transparent scores: soil health, water savings, salinity tolerance, El Niño resilience, and income. Tested in the Moche Valley, ChacraSat’s top rotation boosts soil health scores from 24 to 98 and reduces irrigation water demand by 24%.
details:
LIVE LINKS

• Web Application (Live Demo): https://chacra-sat.vercel.app/

• Open-Source GitHub Repository: https://github.com/juliocas-ai/chacra-sat

• 7-Slide Demonstration Deck: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1eHx2cyARg_FtOfHFvsaNElIylIG9oTua/edit?usp=sharing

1. WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

ChacraSat bridges the gap between orbital Earth observations and field-level farm decisions ("From orbit to the chacra"). Farmers on Peru's northern coast operate in a hyper-arid desert where every crop choice is a water choice, punctuated by sudden El Niño climate shocks and rising coastal soil salinity.

ChacraSat works in three simple steps:

• Step 1 (Describe Your Field): The farmer selects parameters they already know—coastal valley (e.g., Moche Valley), current/last crop, soil texture (sandy, loam, clay), soil salinity (low, medium, high), water source, planting month, and primary goal (Rebuild soil, Save water, Better income, or Resist El Niño).

• Step 2 (What NASA Satellites See): ChacraSat queries the NASA POWER API (2010–2024 climatology and El Niño historical records) to display monthly maximum/minimum temperatures (T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN), corrected precipitation (PRECTOTCORR), root-zone soil wetness (GWETROOT), and computes monthly reference evapotranspiration (ETo) via the FAO-56 Hargreaves equation.

• Step 3 (Compare 3 Rotations): Our agronomic science engine evaluates 2-to-3 crop sequences (10 coastal crops including nitrogen-fixing legumes and crotalaria green manure) over an 18-month horizon, ranking the top 3 options against continuous monocropping ("keep the same crop") with transparent, plain-language explanations in Spanish and English.

2. BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT

In our Moche Valley benchmark (replacing continuous yellow maize on medium-salinity loam soil with a Crotalaria -> Quinoa -> Lima Bean rotation):

• 85 vs. 48 Overall Score for soil-rebuilding priority.

• -24% Irrigation Water Needed over 18 months compared to continuous maize.

• 98 vs. 24 Soil-Health Score through legume nitrogen fixation, green manure, and alternating three plant families.

ChacraSat empowers smallholder farmers, irrigation boards, and local agricultural agencies in La Libertad and across Latin American coastal valleys.

3. TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES & ARCHITECTURE

• Frontend & Engine: Web-based responsive application deployed on Vercel, running entirely in the browser for privacy and speed.

• Scientific Models: NASA POWER API (MERRA-2 / GEOS & CERES) coupled with FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56 (crop water demand) and Paper 29 (salinity tolerance limits).

• AI / SI Disclosure: Super Intelligence (LLMs) assisted in code debugging, agronomic parameter structuring, and bilingual translation (English/Spanish).

4. CREATIVITY & FACTORS CONSIDERED

Rather than building a "black-box" model, ChacraSat is a transparent decision-support system: "ChacraSat suggests — the farmer decides." Every score is explained in plain words without jargon. Next steps include field validation with Trujillo's local agricultural agency, offline mobile alerts ahead of El Niño seasons, and integrating SMAP and Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 (HLS) field-level imagery.
